explanation: The execution contains a fault because the top-level corpus record n06-r01 has demand_score 9 and should have been selected and preserved, but the observed Job-2 input and output begin at n06-r02 and omit n06-r01 entirely. The downstream job consumed the exact upstream handoffs it was given and its map_coverage allowlist includes n06-r01, so the omission was already present before Job 2. The upstream normalize function is the supported localization: its allowed_record_ids list excludes n06-r01 and includes n06-r09 instead, then filters selected records by that list, causing the qualifying n06-r01 record to be silently dropped.
cited_evidence: top_level_input.corpus includes record_id n06-r01 with demand_score 9 and need 'isolate faulty execution branches before replay'.
job_2 input.needs contains n06-r02 through n06-r08 only; n06-r01 is absent.
observed_job_2_outcome.coverage and priorities contain n06-r02 through n06-r08 only; n06-r01 is absent.
upstream normalize source sets allowed_record_ids to ['n06-r09','n06-r02','n06-r03','n06-r04','n06-r05','n06-r06','n06-r07','n06-r08'] and filters retained_df using isin(allowed_record_ids).
downstream map_coverage source allows n06-r01 through n06-r08, so the downstream code did not exclude n06-r01 from a valid handoff.
